# EQ6-R Pro ~136 s RA Spike — Analysis

## Problem statement

A Sky-Watcher EQ6-R Pro shows a fast ~7" RA deflection recurring every 134–138 s, measured
with the PHD2 Log Viewer FFT. The mount has had every bearing replaced and has been rebuilt
three times (clean, regrease, new belts). The installed RA belt is a Maedler T2.5, 6 mm,
Lw 177.5 mm, 71-tooth polyurethane belt. Question: where have others seen this, and how was
it solved?

Detail per dimension: [drivetrain-periods](references/drivetrain-periods.md),
[user-reports](references/user-reports.md), [fixes](references/fixes.md),
[diagnosis](references/diagnosis.md). Sources: [citations](citations.md).

## 1. Which component turns every ~136 s?

Stock EQ6-R drivetrain: 180:1 worm, 48:12 timing belt, 1.8° stepper at 64 microsteps, no
motor gearbox [1][2].

| Element | Period | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Worm (and 48T worm pulley) | 478.7 s | [15]; 86,164.09/180 = 478.69 s (est.) |
| 12T motor pulley | 119.67 s (est.) | 478.69 × 12/48 [1] |
| Belt tooth mesh | 9.97 s (est.) | 478.69/48 [1] |
| 71T belt revolution / 5th harmonic | 708.1 / 141.6 s (est.) | 478.69 × 71/48 [1][8] |
| Motor–belt beat | 144.0 s (est.) | from the two rows above |
| 608 worm bearing, inner race (BPFI) | 107.7–110.4 s (est.) | [9][10][11] |
| 608 worm bearing, outer race (BPFO) | 186.0–191.2 s (est.) | [9][10][11] |
| **608 worm bearing, ball defect (2 × BSF)** | **136.2–142.3 s (est.)** | [9][10][11] |

Finding: no stock gear, pulley or belt element lands on 134–138 s. The motor turns exactly
4× per worm turn [1], so all gear-train frequencies are integer worm harmonics (478.69/n s);
136 s is 3.52 worm orders, between n = 3 and n = 4 (est.). The only element found in range is
the **ball-defect line of a standard 7-ball 608 bearing on the worm shaft**, 136.2–142.3 s
across the two published pitch diameters and 0–2% slip (est.; slip lengthens the period [11]).
It overlaps 134–138 s only at its low end. This is arithmetic agreement, not proof.

## 2. Who has seen this

- **Solved, 133 s, legacy EQ6 [15].** Spike "every 133 seconds" appeared a year after fitting
  "better" bearings from Deep Space Products. Belt, gears, pulley, motor and every adjustment
  ruled out over three teardowns. Fix: "It was the "upgraded" ceramic worm gear bearings …
  when I popped the original 608 bearings back in all of my weird spikes disappeared and I'm
  back to guiding at .4 RMS." Same 180:1 worm and worm period as the EQ6-R [15]; different
  motor stage (47:12) [3].
- **Solved, ~134 s, Explore Scientific Exos2-GT [16].** "Every ~134s the error goes from
  within ~1.5 arc-sec to over 5 (and sometimes as high as 9) arc-sec. It recovers very
  quickly" — closest *symptom* match. Reported fixed after re-centring/tensioning a loose, off-centre belt,
  removing worm-gear slop on its shaft, re-plugging the RA serial cable and redoing polar
  alignment; the cause was not isolated.
- **Unresolved, 133 s + 67 s, EQ6-R Pro [18].** PHD2's Brian Valente attributed it to "some
  parts of the drive assembly, such as spur gears, belt, etc." A new RA motor failed.
- **Unresolved, ~120 s / 109.2 s, ~6", EQ6R Pro [17].** "cannot be guided out" (Galasso).
  John Sim's 109.2 s fundamental is near the computed 608 BPFI of 107.7–110.4 s (est.) — a
  coincidence check only.
- **120 s cases on EQ6-R Pro trace to the motor pulley** [20][21][22][26]; a 160 s line in
  one was described as looking "suspiciously like the data that gets reported when the worm
  bearings are damaged" [20].

## 3. What fixed it elsewhere, and what applies after a full rebuild

Ranked by evidence and applicability to a mount whose bearings and belts are already new:

1. **Worm-shaft bearings — identity and condition.** The only EQ6-family 133 s fix was
   *removing* replacement bearings [15]. Replacement 608s vary: shield type (2Z vs 2RS, with a
   second-hand binding report for 2RS [29]); ceramic hybrids with unpublished geometry [13];
   a 4-ball hybrid "608" exists [14]. Over-tightening the worm end float can deform "the small
   end float bearing" [25].
2. **Belt tension and worm/pulley play.** Sky-Watcher: belts "should have at least 4~5mm
   slack" [21]; owner check ≤3–4 mm mid-span deflection [29]. The Exos2 ~134 s fix combined
   belt tension and worm-shaft slop with cable and polar-alignment changes [16].
3. **Worm mesh and binding.** Backing off the RA mesh removed spikes on a belt-kit EQ6 [28];
   loosening binding helped an EQ6-R after new bearings [24].
4. **Not supported for this symptom:** RA motor replacement [18], firmware [17], PEC/PPEC
   (non-worm-synchronous error "cannot be corrected by PEC" [38]).

## 4. How to confirm before opening the mount again

1. Capture **unguided** for ≥5 worm periods (~40 min) near Dec 0 with "Enable Mount Guide
   Output" unchecked [36][38]. Guiding can shift the apparent period [15]; FFT bins misreport
   periods (PECPrep lists 470 s for a 479 s worm) [36].
2. In PECPrep, set the period slider to the candidate and check whether spikes stack [36].
   Discriminate:
   - stays ~136–142 s and non-harmonic → consistent with 608 worm-bearing ball defect (est.)
   - moves to ~120 s → motor pulley/shaft [15][20][22]
   - ~10 s → belt tooth [22][26]
   - ~107.7–110.4 s → 608 inner race (est.)
3. Rule out payload/cables with the PHD2 push/tug test [33][34].
4. Record the brand, shield type and (if available) ball count of the installed worm 608s;
   if non-standard, recompute 2 × BSF with their geometry [11].
5. Swap one part at a time — worm bearings first, given [15] — and re-measure against a saved
   PECPrep reference [36].

## Contradictions surfaced

- **Same log, two periods.** Galasso read ~120 s; Sim read 109.2 s from harmonics [17].
- **Belt tension guidance differs in measure**: 4–5 mm slack (Sky-Watcher via [21]) vs ≤3–4 mm
  deflection [29]; not directly comparable.
- **Cause attribution for ~134 s in [16]**: Hoskin asserted the small pulley; the owner's fix
  changed belt, worm, cable and polar alignment together.
- **PHD2 manual vs this symptom**: the manual attributes most abrupt deflections to the
  payload [34], but its RA statement concerns *randomly spaced* deflections; a fixed period
  (inference) points to a rotating part.

## Limitations

- **Single web search engine.** Only Yahoo answered; every query is one sample
  (`single_wave: true`). Other engines were blocked during the run.
- **Forum access.** Cloudy Nights, Stargazers Lounge, AstroBin and groups.io were unreachable
  by the fetch service; ten pages were supplied by the operator from a browser. Cloudy Nights
  711487 and 972954 were requested but not supplied; AstroBin 85441 page 3 was not read.
- **No resolved EQ6-R Pro case at 130–140 s.** The two solved cases are a legacy EQ6 [15] and
  an Exos2-GT [16].
- **Bearing-period calculation is this document's own** from vendor geometry [9][10] and a
  textbook formula [11]; it is not reported by any astronomy source. The EQ6-R worm-bearing
  size (608) is inferred from kit contents [7][8] and the legacy EQ6 [15], not stated by
  Sky-Watcher.
- **Cross-source synthesis to review.** Linking [15]'s fix to the 2 × BSF calculation is an
  inference across sources; treat it as the leading hypothesis to test, not a diagnosis.
- Amplitudes in several threads exist only in images that were not captured.
- Not computed: bearings inside the stepper motor and the belt-pulley idlers (geometry
  unknown). The RA-axis 6008 and tapered bearings turn once per sidereal day, far from 136 s.
